The United States delegation to the United Nations exited the General Assembly Hall in New York on Wednesday as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian displayed images of children allegedly killed by United States strikes, Raw Story reported. This move left the Iranian president to finish his address to an empty section of the hall previously occupied by the American team.
The incident occurred during an intense session at the United Nations, taking place just one day after President Donald Trump issued a threat to annihilate Iran from the same podium. President Pezeshkian used his time at the microphone to deliver a sharp condemnation of the current administration. He specifically referenced the recent start of a war against Iran initiated by President Donald Trump.
During his speech, President Pezeshkian addressed the accusations leveled against his country. “Yesterday, the United States president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism,” Pezeshkian said, according to the U.N. live translator. “I come from an Iran in which our esteemed supreme leader was assassinated without any legal framework or reason; I come from an Iran where in truth, they bombed a school.”
President Pezeshkian specifically highlighted the Shajareh Tayyebeh girls’ elementary school
The Shajareh Tayyebeh girls’ elementary school was hit by a double tap strike involving United States-made Tomahawk missiles. Reports indicate that at least 156 people died in that attack, including 120 children.
While President Donald Trump initially attempted to place the blame for the school strike on Iran, subsequent reporting made it clear that the United States was the party responsible. Another strike on a sports hall reportedly resulted in the deaths of 22 civilians and caused significant damage to a nearby school.
President Pezeshkian held up photographs of children he identified as victims of United States military actions. “You see these children? These children perished under bombs with weapons used by the United States and Israel,” Pezeshkian said. He continued his address by detailing the nature of the weapons used in these conflicts.
“They were innocent, had committed no crimes. A sports hall where children were busy playing, the United States, by using weapons with multiple warheads, targeted that sports hall. They martyred, assassinated our scientists, our men, women and children. Innocent children who in truth had committed no crimes, no sins!”
The atmosphere in the General Assembly Hall remained tense as the United States delegation walked out while the president continued his remarks. He concluded his segment by directly challenging the labels applied to his nation. “Those who are terrorists and train and protect terrorists describe us as such,” Pezeshkian stated.
He emphasized his position that his country has only acted in self-defense and is not a terrorist state.

US and Iran Resume Indirect New York Talks as Pezeshkian Tells UN: 'We Did Not Bend the Knee'
The contacts in New York followed months of conflict, while President Masoud Pezeshkian rejected capitulation and called for diplomacy without threats or coercion
Iran and the United States have held mediated talks in New York after nearly seven months of war, as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the United Nations General Assembly that Tehran had 'not bent the knee' to Washington.
The contacts on the sidelines of the UN summit come after a conflict that has continued to affect Iran and the wider region since a June ceasefire collapsed. Pezeshkian, who has advocated diplomacy with the West, is seeking to reopen dialogue with Washington while publicly rejecting any suggestion that Iran is surrendering.
Pezeshkian's UN Show of Defiance
Speaking beneath portraits of Iran's late supreme leader Ali Khamenei and images of more than 150 schoolchildren he said were killed in the conflict's opening days, Pezeshkian portrayed Iran as the victim of US attacks rather than the aggressor.
'We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists,' he told delegates, accusing the United States and Israel of 'cowardly attacks and aggressions' against Iranian civilians.
His most pointed remark was blunt: 'Yes, they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee.' He added that Iran remained 'ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force'.
However, Pezeshkian's claim that Iran had only defended itself comes amid Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the region. The latest incident involved a cargo ship struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in two casualties, while the crew abandoned the vessel.
The speech came less than 24 hours after President Trump warned from the same podium that he might 'annihilate' the Islamic Republic absent a deal, framing his choice as one between allowing Iran to rebuild or destroying it 'quickly'.
Trump later moderated his tone, telling reporters there had been 'a very good meeting' between envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Iranian officials, though he noted the Iranians present were 'not the highest level'.
Tehran played down the contact. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the exchange was 'not anything new', reiterating Iran's longstanding demands that Washington lift its naval blockade and unfreeze Iranian assets.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump remained open to a deal that let Iran become 'a great and prosperous country', but blamed Iran's nuclear programme and alleged support for terrorism for the impasse, warning that 'a number of options', including further military action, remained on the table.
Hormuz Blast Clouds Tehran's Message
Pezeshkian's attempt to present Iran as a responsible actor was complicated by events at sea. The UK Maritime Trade Operations body reported that a cargo ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz was struck on Wednesday by an unidentified projectile, resulting in two casualties, while the crew abandoned the vessel.
Commercial traffic through the strait, which carried roughly a fifth of the world's traded oil before the war, remains well below prewar levels, with some vessels reportedly disabling their identification systems to evade rival blockades.
Conflict Spreads From Gaza to Diplomacy
The wider region offered little respite. Gaza's Health Ministry said an Israeli strike in Khan Younis killed two people on Wednesday, including a man Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz identified as a senior Hamas finance official. The ministry says more than 1,400 Palestinians have died since a ceasefire began nearly a year ago.
Separately, Israel accused French President Emmanuel Macron of 'grotesque absurdity' after he told the UN that Hamas had never been active in the West Bank.
A French diplomatic official later clarified that Macron meant Hamas does not govern the territory, while Hamas has maintained a presence in the West Bank and has been linked to attacks there.

Lashing back at Trump at UN, Iranian leader calls US and Israel the aggressors
At the U.N. General Assembly, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded Wednesday to President Donald Trump’s threats from the day before and defended his country’s nuclear program.
His voice rising, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian delivered a furious rebuke Wednesday of U.S. President Donald Trump, who, from the very same podium at the United Nations General Assembly 24 hours earlier, had threatened to wipe out his country.
“The U.S. president described us as terrorists,” Mr. Pezeshkian told world leaders. “We have been victims of terrorism,” he added, just before waving photos of Iranian schoolgirls killed in a U.S. airstrike on Feb. 28, the day the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran.
Mr. Pezeshkian began his speech at the annual summit by holding up a photo of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the Iranian supreme leader who also was killed on the first day of strikes.
Continuing a war of words begun a day earlier before the United Nations General Assembly, Iran’s president snapped back at the United States and Israel by claiming, “We have been victims of terrorism.”
He quickly unleashed against Israel, Iran’s longtime archfoe, describing its actions in the Gaza war as genocide. He repeated the Iranian argument that the Islamic Republic seeks nuclear technology for civilian and not military purposes – “for progress, not to threaten societies with weapons.”
And he accused Israel of building a nuclear bomb, but without the international repercussions and sanctions his country has faced. “The nuclear weapon is in Israel, but the inspectors are in Iran,” he said. Israel has never confirmed or denied having nuclear weapons, but for decades has maintained it would not be the first country in the region to use such weapons.
Mr. Trump vowed in his U.N. address on Tuesday that he would never let Iran secure nuclear weapons. Preventing Tehran, which has threatened to wipe Israel off the map, from developing a bomb was the chief stated aim for going to war.
Mr. Pezeshkian presented Iran as seeking peace and stability, drawn into a war of self-defense by the U.S. and Israel, whom he described as the real aggressors and agents of instability.
“They imposed the war on us, but we have proven we are not afraid of war,” he said. “We will not bow our heads and give up the right inherently ours. We say clearly no nuclear weapons and no limitations to nuclear technology.”
His remarks included no mention of Iran’s sponsorship of its allies in what has been dubbed the “Axis of Resistance,” which includes Hezbollah, Hamas, and the Houthis in Yemen, all defined as terror organizations by the U.S.
Mr. Pezeshkian’s very presence in New York is remarkable for more than one reason. It marks the first time in history that the leader of a country at war with the United States has attended the U.N. General Assembly. And Mr. Pezeshkian has been criticized at home by Iran’s powerful hard-liners for a willingness to negotiate, or even to go to New York.
Reflecting the fine line he’s walking, he concluded his speech to applause in the hall, saying, “We will never bow our heads or bend our knees. We are ready for dialogue, diplomacy and negotiations, but will never accept the language of force.”
Despite the defiant U.S. and Iranian exchanges, Mr. Trump confirmed that U.S. and Iranian representatives did meet Tuesday on the sidelines of the U.N. gathering.
